newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil police arrest Colombian drug trafficker.
newsitem.headline: Brazil police arrest Colombian drug trafficker.

text.p: Brazilian police have arrested a Colombian drug trafficker who is wanted in the United States as she was trying to enter Brazil with a false passport, a police spokesman said on Thursday.
He said Mery Valencia, travelling on a fake Spanish passport under the name of Luz Mary Vallejo Mena, was arrested on Feb. 7 at Rio de Janeiro's international airport.
"She was arrested on charges of using false documents and on detention orders resulting from an extradition request by the United States," the spokesman said. "She was identified via fingerprints."
Valencia is due to go on trial in the United States in July on charges of international drug trafficking, the spokesman said. The extradition process is expected to take four to five months.

The FBI accuses her of the sale and distribution of 20 to 25 metric tons of cocaine in the United States between 1986 and 1992, he said. She is believed to have drug trafficking and money-laundering ties with Colombia's Cali and Medellin drug cartels.

The United States issued an extradition request before Valencia arrived in Brazil because the FBI suspected she would visit Rio de Janeiro for February's annual carnival celebrations, as she had done in the past, the spokesman said.
